æcse, adsan, bil, byrse, scafan, sage, cimbiren, tigehoc, næfebor, mattuc, ippingiren, scear, culter and eac gadiren, siðe, sicol, weodhoc, spade, scofle, wadspitel, bærwan, besman, bytel, race, geafle, hlædre, horscamb and sceara, fyrtange, wæipundern. [15] Axt, Beil, Hippe, Bohrer, Hobel, Säge, Kimmeisen [Böttcherbeil], Ziehhaken, Naber [= Bohrer], Hacke, Brecheisen[?], Pflugschar, Kolter und auch Stachelstock, Sense, Sichel, Unkrauthacke, Spaten, Schaufel, Waidhacke, Tragebahre, Besen, Stössel, Rechen, [Heu-]Gabel, Leiter, Pferdekamm und [grosse Wirthschafts-]Scheere, Feuerzange, Wage mit Gewicht; [15.1] und viele Spinngeräthe: Flachsleine, Spindel, Haspel, Garnwinde, Rietkamm des Webstuhls, Zeugbäume, [Tuch]presse, Weberkamm, Karden..?, Einschlag, Kette [oder Schiffchen], Wollkamm, Webebaum, Webespule [oder Riedblatt], Haspelstock, Schiffchen[?], ‘Saumstöcke’, kleine Scheere, Nadel, Schlägel.

[15] Axe, adze, bill, borer, plane, saw, chime-iron [cooper's axe], drawing-hook, auger, mattock, crowbar[?], ploughshare, coulter and also goad, scythe, sickle, weed-hook, spade, shovel, woad-dibble, barrow, broom, beetle, rake, [hay-]fork, ladder, horse-comb and [large household] shears, fire-tongs, scales with weights; [15.1] and many spinning implements: flax-line, spindle, reel, yarn-winder, stodles [loom uprights], beams, press, comb, carders(?), weft, warp [or shuttle], wool-comb, loom-roller, slay [or reed], winding-stick, shuttle[?], seam-sticks, small shears, needle, beater.

Axe, adze, billhook, chisel, plane, saw, joining iron, hook for earthenware vessels, auger, mattock, crowbar, ploughshare, coulter, and also a goad, scythe, sickle, weed-hook (hoe), spade, shovel, woad-dibble, barrow, broom, mallet, rake, fork, ladder, horse-comb, scissors, fire tongs, weighing scale and many spinning implements, a cord for hanging flax from, spindle, reel, yarn winder, weaver’s slay, distaff, clothes’ press, loom parts, [weavers’ instrument], [weavers’ instrument], [weavers’ instrument], wool comb, weaver’s beam, pail, [weaver’s instrument], shuttle, harness, [weaver’s instrument], shears, needle, mallet.

ax, adze, billhook, chisel, plane, saw, clamp, pull hook, auger, mattock, crowbar, plowshare, coulter, and likewise a goad, scythe, sickle, hoe, spade, shovel, woad dibble, barrow, broom, mallet, rake, fork, ladder, horse comb and shears, fire tongs, scale. [15.1] Also many spinning tools: a line for hanging flax, spindle, reel, yarn winders, loom uprights, heddle rods, a cloth press, comb beater, temples, weft thread, warp thread, wool comb, yoke beam, beater, crank, sheath, seam picks, fabric shears, needle, wooden mallet.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 15–15.1. B's ‘næfebor’ stands so. Liebermann's translations of the rarer terms are marked with queries; the English follows his German.
This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (15, 15.1), each marked with its number.

[15.1] spinning tools: The implements listed here have occasioned considerable critical head-scratching. Though some are recognizable tools still in use, others remain obscure. The confusion is exacerbated by the fact that many of the terms in this list occur nowhere else in Old English.
